status: DRAFT generator config (P0-CORRIDOR-REFERENCE) - finalize in P1-GEN-REFERENCE after P0-DATA-CONTRACTS

lineage.endpoint_rule: site_a/site_z = lowest-id active central_office per city; metro and diverse routes use lowest-id data_center (fallback: next site) as 2nd endpoint
lineage.origin_values: MIXED = source row + twin attributes; SYNTHETIC = generated

corridor_id_format: <CITY_A>-<CITY_Z> alphabetical 3-letter codes (DEN,SLC,CHI,DAL,ASH,SEA,ATL,PHX); metro = <CITY>-MET; diverse = <base>-D2. Acceptance query 2 keys on corridor_id='DEN-SLC'.
capacity_gbps_rule: long-haul fiber_count >=1500 -> 19200, >=600 -> 9600, else 4800; metro 4800; diverse 4800; DEN-SLC fixed 9600

utilization.non_anomaly_rule: baseline = source avg_peak_util_pct*100 - 10 +/- 6, capped at 70; end = baseline + U(0,6); max non-DEN-SLC end util = 72.6 so DEN-SLC is the only corridor exhausting within 6 months

DEN-SLC_EXHAUSTION.name: DEN-SLC RapidRoute
DEN-SLC_EXHAUSTION.note: Concave AI-growth curve; extrapolating the same curve crosses 95% at t=210 (2027-03-16). Use as corridor-level 7-day mean target for telemetry_span_hourly on DEN-SLC spans and as the ground truth P3-FORECAST-MODEL should reproduce.

SRLG-88_DIVERSE_PAIR.note: Recommendation for P1-GEN-TOPOLOGY: spans sold as diverse routes but share conduit SRLG-88.

source_data_issues: silver_corridor.total_distance_km is a sum of segment lengths for many long-haul keys (e.g. Dallas-Phoenix 35543 km). Rule: long-haul distance_km = great-circle(endpoint sites) x 1.25 route factor (x1.12 more for diverse -D2 routes); source value retained in source_distance_km. Metro rings keep source distance.
geographic_site.site_name uses 'LakeLink' casing; twin display names use 'Lakelink Fiber'
